title: Demonstration guide: education
content: To review educational background, look for an institution-issued biography or an official résumé. Record the qualification, institution, year, and original source. No qualification is established in this demonstration.

title: Demonstration guide: career
content: To review political experience, build a dated timeline from original records. Distinguish elected office, appointed office, and candidacy. No office history is established in this demonstration.

title: Demonstration guide: legislation
content: Look beyond a bill’s title. Separate what a senator filed, what they sponsored, and what became law. Read the full text, authorship, legislative status, and related journal. Keep the congressional period consistent when comparing records.

title: Demonstration guide: bills
content: Authorship and sponsorship are different roles. Check the author list and sponsorship record separately, then read the bill text and its latest status. Filing a bill does not establish that it became law. No bill or resolution is attributed to this senator in this demonstration.

title: Demonstration guide: committees
content: Check a dated committee roster and distinguish chair, vice-chair, and member roles. Membership can change during a congressional period. No committee role is confirmed in this demonstration.

title: Demonstration guide: votes
content: Check the roll-call record, measure, date, and voting stage together. Absence, abstention, and a vote against a measure are different records. No individual vote is confirmed in this demonstration.

title: Demonstration guide: statements
content: Read the complete original statement with its date and context. Distinguish a direct quotation from a paraphrase or interpretation. This demonstration contains no quotations attributed to a senator.

title: Demonstration guide: positions
content: A documented position needs an attributable statement or record about a specific issue. Do not infer a stance from party membership or missing information. No senator’s position is established in this demonstration.

title: Demonstration guide: procedures
content: When exploring Senate procedures, follow a measure through filing, committee consideration, plenary deliberation, and subsequent action. Use the current rules and the original journal to confirm the exact procedure. This is a generic demonstration guide.
